segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Biden's new job numbers are out, and they are ugly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In short, real jobs are down, while DoorDash and government jobs are the entire Bidenomics

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: miracle.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: My colleague EJ and Tony broke it down in a Twitter thread, so let's dig in.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Headline jobs rose 209,000 in the June report, which was 30,000 less than expected, so that's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: a mess.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: That's also the lowest in two and a half years, and it took the unemployment rate to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: 3.6%, which is up just a smidge on the year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Meanwhile, the previous two months were revised down by 110,000 jobs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: By the way, we've seen this every report this year with numbers being revised down, meaning

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: either government statisticians are getting very bad at their job, or they are intentionally

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: reporting rosy numbers, then revising them down when nobody is looking.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So accounting for the revisions leaves about 100,000 jobs on the month.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Keep in mind, population growth cancels about 70,000 of those, leaving 30,000, essentially

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: flat on a worker population of 162 million.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: But it gets worse.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: For starters, most of those net jobs were actually government jobs, which don't grow the economy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In fact, many shrink it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: We can debate whether an EPA bureaucrat cancels 5 or 10 workers, but they certainly aren't growing

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: anything.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: They are parasites.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So that takes us to productive jobs growing actually below the pace of population.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Finally, the big one, job composition.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: The BLS reported that multiple job holders rose an amazing 233,000 on the month, which completely

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: swamped the alleged job gains.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In addition, 452,000 more people were working part-time for, quote, economic reasons.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In other words, not by choice, which BLS attributes to people whose, quote, hours were reduced due

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: to slack work or business conditions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In other words, companies are reducing hours, which is the next step to layoffs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Take it together, and real jobs plunged by over 100,000 with more to come, while Americans made

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: up the difference delivering DoorDash, not even counting the 2 million-plus workers who

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: are still missing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: I've mentioned in previous videos that they've dropped out of the labor force since COVID.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Many are now on government benefits, where they're no longer counted as unemployed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Statistically, they're retired.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So what's next?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Erosion and job composition is hitting wages, which came in flat after inflation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: That's actually surprising, since inflation was supposed to have trickled into wages by now.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: I've got an upcoming video on that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Even so, flat wages is bad news for the Fed, who's trying to make wages go down so people

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: stop spending and the federal government can spend instead.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So expect the Fed to turn this into yet more rate hikes, limited at this point only by their

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: fear of crashing yet more banks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Month by month, Americans are losing their financial buffer, their full-time jobs, their savings,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: all while their debts pile up amid Washington happy talk about the amazing feats of Bidenomics.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: As post-pandemic pent-up demand fades and the economy drops into full-blown recession,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: on present trends, there will be millions of Americans up against the wall.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Okay, we'll be watching.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: See you next time.
